text: But if he'd known YOU, I'm sure he would have felt quite different. I shall tell him about you.” “What shall you tell him?” “I shall tell him,” said Fauntleroy, glowing with enthusiasm, “that you are the kindest man I ever heard of. And you are always thinking of other people, and making them happy and--and I hope when I grow up, I shall be just like you.” “Just like me!” repeated his lordship, looking at the little kindling face. And a dull red crept up under his withered skin, and he suddenly turned his eyes away and looked out of the carriage window at the great beech-trees, with the sun shining on their glossy, red-brown leaves. “JUST like you,” said Fauntleroy, adding modestly, “if I can.
